references.text: The preceding verse promises God's blessing in the sixth year so that the harvest will last for three years, which is the prerequisite for what is described in verse 22.
Describes the Sabbath-year regulations about letting the land rest, which is the background for why the people had to eat from old crops.
Parallel text about eating old produce (יָשָׁן) and having to clear away the old to make room for new, showing God's abundant blessing.
The promise of the Lord's blessing over storehouses and all work, which supports trust in God's provision during the Sabbath year.
The manna gathered on the sixth day lasted two days, a similar principle of God's provision when His people obey His Sabbath ordinances.
Jesus' teaching not to worry about food and drink but to trust that the heavenly Father knows what we need—the same principle of trust as in the Sabbath year.
The Israelites ate from the land's produce after entering Canaan, and the manna ceased—an transition from old to new harvest.
